items.stem: Claude suggests an analysis method that produces a striking result. Before presenting it, you should:

options.text: Reproduce the result from the raw data and check the method fits
options.rationale: Correct: a result must be reproducible and the method appropriate before use.

options.text: Present it because the result is compelling
options.rationale: A compelling result can still be a methodological artefact.

options.text: Ask Claude to confirm it is correct
options.rationale: The model's self-confirmation is not verification.

options.text: Round the result to make it look more cautious
options.rationale: Rounding does not validate the underlying analysis.

items.explanation: Correct: a result must be reproducible and the method appropriate before use.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO things should an analytical output show to be honest? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The assumptions the analysis relies on
options.rationale: Correct: readers must know what the result depends on.

options.text: The data source and its as-of date
options.rationale: Correct: provenance and currency let the reader judge the result.

options.text: The maximum number of decimal places possible
A headline number with no context

items.stem: A call to the Anthropic API fails with a transient error. What is the appropriate handling?

options.text: Retry with backoff a bounded number of times, then surface the error
options.rationale: Correct: bounded retries handle transient faults without hiding real failures.

options.text: Crash the whole app so the user notices
options.rationale: Crashing on a transient fault is a poor user experience.
Unbounded immediate retries worsen load and can hang the app.
Hiding the failure produces misleading empty output.

items.explanation: Correct: bounded retries handle transient faults without hiding real failures.
